newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf states 1996 oil revenues seen at $90 billion.
newsitem.headline: Gulf states 1996 oil revenues seen at $90 billion.

text.p: Higher world oil prices will lift Gulf Arab states' oil revenue to about $90 billion this year from $78 billion in 1995, the Emirates Industrial Bank said Sunday.
"(This) will contribute to a decrease in budget deficits and encourage the economic positions in these countries in general," the bank said in its latest economic report.
The oil-rich Gulf states are Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest crude oil producer, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman.
Oil is currently trading near its highest level since the 1991 Gulf War.
